content.comment_body: Dear Expert [user_name], I hope this message finds you well. I'm experiencing a similar issue. I can't connect [product_name] to my PC running Windows 7. I use the driver for the USB cable provided by setup.exe ([product_name] Comfort [version_no]). The connection works once after booting Windows, then consistently drops with the same error, always in online test mode. Most of the time, I can't connect at all. I'm sure the cable is correct, since with this version of [product_name] Comfort under Windows XP, it works flawlessly. I would appreciate it if you could let me know the possible cause. Best regards, [user_name]. P.S. Can I get your answer here or should I start a new thread?

Hello, When you mention only online test, do you mean upload and download functions work properly? Which version of [product_name] do you have? Can you share a screenshot from Help > About > System Info? Perhaps you need to install a new version of Java; I don't have Windows 7 available to check settings. I've had problems with online test on some [product_name] versions as well, but it worked after uploading. Regards,

Hi, Try setting the correct [product_name] version in your software. Many users create programs for older [product_name] units and forget to select the appropriate model when downloading to a newer one. Download usually works, but online test often doesn't. For example, if you're using [product_name] [article_no], select [product_name] [article_no] ES3 in the settings. Otherwise, online test won't function properly. The same applies to newer versions. Hope this helps.

I am having the same concern. I have [product_name] ([article_no]) and a laptop, but cannot establish communication. I connected the [product_name] via ethernet cable and it has its own power supply. Please advise how to connect or configure [product_name] to communicate with a laptop running Windows 7.

Hello, Please refer to the attached [document] for guidance on setting up both your [product_name] hardware and associated software. The [document] is also available in the [product_name] application examples. Ensure your PC IP address is in the same subnet range as your device (only the last number should differ) and the subnet mask matches. Regards,

Dear Expert [user_name], Thank you in advance for your response. Sorry if my initial explanation was unclear. I didn't mean 'only at online test.' My main issue is that most of the time I cannot connect to any [product_name] version (including [article_no], [article_no], but not yet [article_no]) using [product_name] Comfort software under Windows 7. Often, I need several attempts to establish a connection for upload/download, and if successful, it disconnects again within about one minute during online test mode. However, with the same hardware under Windows XP, everything works seamlessly. Thank you again for your support and guidance. Best regards, [user_name]. P.S. Special thanks to [user_name]_Moderator for creating this thread.

Hello [user_name], When working with my program (.lsc extension) under Windows XP, everything functioned perfectly (upload/download and online test mode). Is your suggested solution specific to Windows 7, or is it a general workaround? Thank you.
Dear Sirs, I hope you are all well. I'm continuing to experience issues with Windows 7 as explained above. Are there any recommendations? All suggestions are welcome. Best regards, [user_name].
Did you attempt to reinstall the driver? If not, uninstall the [product_name] USB driver, download the latest version from [url], and install it anew. Regards, [user_name]
Dear [user_name], Thank you for your response. I did try reinstalling—the driver reinstallation was my first troubleshooting step. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users report unstable and unreliable connections between [product_name] devices and PCs using [product_name] Comfort [version_no] on Windows 7. While the same setup works reliably on Windows XP, connection attempts, especially in online test mode, fail frequently or disconnect after a minute across several [product_name] versions using USB and Ethernet. The recurring issues indicate Windows 7-specific driver or compatibility problems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect consistent and reliable communication, including stable online test functionality, between [product_name] hardware and PCs running Windows 7—similar to seamless operation observed on Windows XP.
